edges.description: A sustained malignant ventricular arrhythmia abolishes effective cardiac output, which is the route by which coronary spasm causes sudden cardiac arrest.

Smoking acts through oxidative inactivation of endothelium-derived nitric oxide. It is a recognized risk factor for vasospastic angina and is placed at the endothelial node because oxidative stress from tobacco smoke consumes nitric oxide and impairs endothelium-dependent dilation. The cited review establishes the risk-factor status; the oxidative route is the proposed mechanism rather than a separately evidenced one here.

The same review groups smoking with low-grade inflammation as the leading risk factors, so smoking is also linked to the adventitial inflammatory node that upregulates Rho-kinase. The connecting steps are not established in this entry's sources and are recorded as unknown.
